items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The main logic is clear, but `if DNS_NAME is not None: ... else: domain = None` adds a check for a case that never happens (DNS_NAME is a module-level CachedDnsName instance). In tests, `from unittest.mock import patch` sits apart from the other stdlib imports.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` is copied into both utils.get_fqdn and message.py. There is no shared helper and existing call sites are not reused. The `is not None` branch is dead code, and with the cached DNS_NAME the second conversion is redundant.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No errors are swallowed and no magic constants are added. IDNA errors (e.g. labels that are too long) are raised, not hidden, which matches the reference. ASCII and empty hostnames were checked to pass through unchanged.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: It converts at the source (`socket.getfqdn().encode('idna')`), works for every encoding and leaves ASCII names unchanged. But it repeats the idna conversion inline in message.py (`str(DNS_NAME).encode('idna')`), so the same conversion lives in two places, even though it is idempotent.
